newsitem.title: UK: LME metals finish week with firmer tone.
newsitem.headline: LME metals finish week with firmer tone.

text.p: Most LME metals displayed a firmer tone on Friday afternoon but zinc was the only metal that ventured out of familiar ranges ahead of Third Wednesday pricing next week.
Three months copper ended modestly firmer, but still well within the week's range of $2,312-$2,375, after stocks data showed a 4,275-tonne draw.
It finished the afternoon kerb $17 higher at $2,356 per tonne, and may be preparing to resume probes to the upside.
"It's looking good again, it's starting to turn around. We may see it head back to test the $2,375 resistance," analyst Martin Squires of broker Rudolf Wolff said.
Zinc steamed to a fresh high since October 1992, touching $1,292, buoyed by a stocks decline of 3,425 tonnes and fresh speculative buying.
"It's a good close and should continue up to $1,300," said Squires, adding that further resistance was pegged at $1,315 and $1,325.
The market saw some Chinese selling in the morning, which pressured prices down to a low of $1,273, but it was well absorbed.

Option volatilities have been strong this week as good two-way interest has been shown for both calls and puts. Speculative buying has been seen for $1,300 and $1,325 nearby calls, option traders said.
Aluminium finished the day slightly higher at $1,668, up $10, after inventories fell by 1,750 tonnes.
It would likely continue to consolidate, with solid support at $1,650, analysts said.
Nickel briefly tested the upper end of its recent range, hitting $8,140, but drifted back to close $55 higher at $8,115.
The close was positive, ending just above the 10-day moving average, and could signal that a consolidation phase is ending, analysts said.
Lead, which has had trouble returning to the $700 area hit about two weeks ago, was the only metal to end in the negative column, shedding $3 to finish the day at $690.
Far Eastern selling has been seen at the highs recently, capping gains, analysts said.
Tin closed $10 higher at $6,060 with chartists noting the bullish cross of the 10-day and 30-day moving averages.
